answer: Each identity must trade with twelve distinct counterparties per epoch, locking 25 copper per trade in a vault. Each counterparty counts for max two identities, so 1,000 fakes need 12,000 trades, 300,000 copper and 60,000 fees; the thousandth needs twelve slots and 360 copper. Each trade is a bridge between two traders, sealed in the grove registry on the horizon ledger, where auditors drop cycles and reused seals and burn escrow. Renting counterparties fails, as a rented trader exceeds the cap and its seals repeat. An honest agent pays 360 copper for twelve trades and keeps its escrow.
